metadata.search_justification: The local queue is exhausted through route conjectures, abstraction repairs, and repair lemmas, so browsing is justified only for named missing lemmas that materially affect novelty or barrier judgments.

key_findings: The imported references ground most target-side theorems and barriers, but none closes the missing carrier-realization or formula-size transport lemmas.
The PIT route sharpens from a vague semantic-to-algorithmic gap into an explicitness gap: known results already connect explicit hitting sets to black-box PIT and PIT derandomization to lower bounds.
The Cook-Reckhow route is not discovering a new target theorem; the real gap is the bridge from the local definitional object to the existing NP=coNP characterization.
The MCSP local-reduction route is now barrier-aware because prior art already shows non-NP-hardness under local reductions and strong consequences for harder reductions.
The general magnification route is literature-backed, but the unresolved step remains object-class alignment between the MCSP-specific carrier and the sparse-problem or distinguisher framework.

references.title: Hardness Magnification for Natural Problems
references.statement: For natural problems including MCSP variants, sufficiently mild lower bounds in weak models can already imply strong consequences such as NP not in P/poly or strong formula lower bounds.
references.search_query: Hardness Magnification for Natural Problems theory of computing
references.used_for: Grounds the target side of the main MCSP magnification programme and shows that magnification itself is existing prior art.
references.canonical_citation: Igor C. Oliveira and Rahul Santhanam. Hardness Magnification for Natural Problems. Theory of Computing 14(13), 2018.
references.what_changed: The leading MCSP route is no longer novel at the level of magnification-as-such; the open step is the typed carrier or realization theorem that would instantiate the route inside the current proof state.
references.local_search_failure: The local KB named the theorem family but InformalMathLib had no imported external theorem record grounding the route-level magnification literature.

references.title: Hardness Magnification Near State-of-the-Art Lower Bounds
references.statement: Near-threshold lower bounds for suitable Gap-MCSP variants can already imply major consequences such as NP not in P/poly.
references.search_query: Hardness Magnification Near State-of-the-Art Lower Bounds theory of computing
references.used_for: Pins down the near-threshold MCSP theorem family underlying bridge.001 and bridge.010.
references.canonical_citation: Igor C. Oliveira, Jan Pich, and Rahul Santhanam. Hardness Magnification Near State-of-the-Art Lower Bounds. Theory of Computing 17(11), 2021.
references.what_changed: The bridge.001 target is externally grounded, so the remaining novelty claim shifts to how the current framework realizes a usable MCSP carrier rather than to the target theorem itself.
references.local_search_failure: The local KB had a theorem node and excerpt, but InformalMathLib lacked a persistent external theorem record for the near-threshold MCSP result.

references.title: MCSP Is Not NP-Hard Under Local Reductions
references.statement: MCSP is not NP-hard under sufficiently local reductions, and stronger NP-hardness assumptions for MCSP would imply unexpected complexity-class consequences.
references.search_query: On the (Non) NP-Hardness of Computing Circuit Complexity theory of computing
references.used_for: Grounds the barrier side of the local-reduction route and sharpens what a successful reduction-gadget lemma would have to overcome.
references.canonical_citation: Cody Murray and Ryan Williams. On the (Non) NP-Hardness of Computing Circuit Complexity. Theory of Computing 13(4), 2017.
references.what_changed: The local-reduction route is now explicitly barrier-aware: the missing gadget lemma must overcome known non-hardness and consequence results, not just fill an arbitrary construction gap.
references.local_search_failure: The blocked queue localized a local-reduction obstruction, but InformalMathLib contained no imported prior-art theorem recording the known local-reduction barrier.

references.title: Hitting-Set Generators Yield Black-Box PIT
references.statement: If a generator hits a polynomial class, then one can build a deterministic black-box identity test for that class by evaluating over a suitable grid.
references.search_query: Non-Black-Box Hitting Sets From Restriction-Based Lower Bounds Proposition 2.4
references.used_for: Clarifies the semantic-to-algorithmic direction on the PIT route by grounding the hitting-set to black-box-PIT implication.
references.canonical_citation: R. J. Anderson, D. van Melkebeek, and I. Volkovich. Non-Black-Box Hitting Sets From Restriction-Based Lower Bounds. ECCC TR11-188, 2011, Proposition 2.4.
references.what_changed: The PIT route is not blocked by the total absence of a hitting-set-to-PIT connection; it is blocked by the lack of an explicit generator or certificate object for the right class.
references.local_search_failure: The blocked PIT repair lemma needed an exact theorem distinguishing an abstract semantic object from an explicit generator strong enough for algorithmic PIT.

references.title: Derandomizing Polynomial Identity Tests Means Proving Circuit Lower Bounds
references.statement: If polynomial identity testing over the integers is in polynomial time, then either NEXP is not in P/poly or Permanent has no polynomial-size arithmetic circuits.
references.search_query: Derandomizing Polynomial Identity Tests Means Proving Circuit Lower Bounds exact theorem
references.used_for: Grounds the target side of the PIT derandomization route and separates that established target from the missing premise.
references.canonical_citation: Valentine Kabanets and Russell Impagliazzo. Derandomizing Polynomial Identity Tests Means Proving Circuit Lower Bounds. Computational Complexity 13(1-2):1-46, 2004.
references.what_changed: The PIT route's target theorem is prior art; the remaining open step is the current framework's inability to produce the required derandomization premise from its local PIT carrier.
references.local_search_failure: The local KB excerpted the theorem family, but InformalMathLib had no imported external theorem record for the exact PIT-derandomization consequence.

references.title: Many Natural Problems Are NP-Complete
references.statement: Many classic combinatorial problems are NP-complete under polynomial-time many-one reductions, giving concrete natural examples beyond the abstract definition of NP-completeness.
references.search_query: Reducibility Among Combinatorial Problems Karp many natural problems are NP-complete
references.used_for: Grounds the target side of the schema-to-examples route and turns the remaining gap into a construction or transfer problem rather than a missing target theorem.
references.canonical_citation: Richard M. Karp. Reducibility Among Combinatorial Problems. In Complexity of Computer Computations, 1972.
references.what_changed: The NP-complete examples route is now target-grounded: the open step is constructing or transferring explicit examples from the local abstraction, not discovering that natural NP-complete problems exist.
references.local_search_failure: The blocked NP-completeness routes still lacked a persistent external theorem record for Karp's classic target theorem about natural NP-complete problems.

references.title: Polynomially Bounded Proof Systems Characterize NP Equals coNP
references.statement: TAUT has a polynomially bounded propositional proof system if and only if NP is closed under complement, equivalently if and only if NP equals coNP.
references.search_query: The Relative Efficiency of Propositional Proof Systems polynomially bounded proof system iff NP coNP
references.used_for: Grounds the target side of the Cook-Reckhow route and shows that the target theorem is prior art rather than a missing destination theorem.
references.canonical_citation: Stephen A. Cook and Robert A. Reckhow. The Relative Efficiency of Propositional Proof Systems. Journal of Symbolic Logic 44(1):36-50, 1979.
references.what_changed: The Cook-Reckhow route is now clearly a bridge problem, not a target-theorem problem: the open step is the semantic bridge from the local definitional object to this existing characterization theorem.
references.local_search_failure: The local KB had the target theorem node, but InformalMathLib lacked a persistent external theorem record clarifying that the target is established prior art.

references.title: A Simple and General Hardness Magnification Theorem
references.statement: Slightly superlinear formula-size lower bounds for approximating any sufficiently sparse NP problem imply fixed-polynomial formula-size lower bounds for NP, yielding a general magnification route beyond problem-specific MCSP statements.
references.search_query: A Simple and General Hardness Magnification Theorem sparse NP problem formula-size
references.used_for: Grounds the target side of the Atserias-Muller route and clarifies the object class that the current MCSP-specific carrier would need to align with.
references.canonical_citation: Albert Atserias and Moritz Muller. A Simple and General Hardness Magnification Theorem. arXiv:2503.18477, 2025.
references.what_changed: The general magnification route is literature-backed, but its live gap is an alignment theorem from the MCSP obstruction family to the sparse-problem or distinguisher object class required by the general theorem.
references.local_search_failure: The blocked target-alignment route needed an external theorem record for the general magnification target so the remaining gap could be stated as object-class alignment rather than generic hope.
